title: Introduce legacy authentication adapter
author: eng-team
description: Introduced a legacy authentication adapter to bridge internal session auth with early enterprise SSO integrations that predate our standard OAuth flow.
decision: Keep a dedicated adapter layer rather than forcing all tenants onto a single auth path immediately.
constraints: Must remain backward compatible with tenants onboarded before OAuth flow existed.
outcome: Adapter shipped; several enterprise tenants onboarded against it.

title: Reviewer flags adapter as temporary
author: reviewer-2
description: PR review comment notes the adapter is meant to be temporary until all tenants can migrate to the standard OAuth flow.
decision: Approved with a follow-up ticket to track eventual removal.
constraints: No committed removal date; blocked on tenant migration.
outcome: Ticket created but deprioritized for over a year.

title: First attempt to migrate all tenants to standard OAuth flow
author: eng-team
description: First large-scale attempt to move every tenant off the legacy adapter and onto the standard OAuth flow.
decision: Roll out OAuth flow to all tenants in a single coordinated cutover.
constraints: Enterprise SSO tenants required custom claim mapping not yet supported by the new flow.
outcome: Migration proceeded without a staged rollback plan.

title: Authentication failures during OAuth cutover
author: on-call
description: Multiple enterprise SSO tenants experienced authentication failures within hours of the OAuth cutover. Root cause: claim mapping mismatch not covered by the new flow.
decision: Emergency rollback to legacy adapter for affected tenants.
constraints: Rollback required re-enabling legacy adapter code paths that were partially removed.
outcome: Service restored after rollback; incident lasted approximately 3 hours.

title: Postmortem: OAuth cutover incident
author: eng-team
description: Postmortem concludes the migration was not validated against enterprise SSO tenant claim mappings before cutover, and no staged rollback existed.
decision: Require tenant-by-tenant compatibility verification before any future adapter removal.
constraints: Any future migration must include a verified rollback path.
outcome: Postmortem action items filed; compatibility verification becomes a stated requirement.

title: Formal architecture decision: adapter stays until tenant verification
author: architecture-review-board
description: Formal architecture decision record stating the legacy authentication adapter must remain in place until all dependent enterprise SSO tenants are individually verified as migration-compatible.
decision: Do not remove the legacy adapter without documented tenant compatibility verification.
constraints: Applies to any future removal or refactor of auth/legacy_adapter.py.

title: Enterprise tenant onboarding still depends on legacy adapter
author: solutions-eng
description: Three additional enterprise customers onboarded using the legacy adapter because their identity providers required claim formats not supported by the standard OAuth flow.
decision: Continue supporting the adapter for enterprise SSO onboarding.
constraints: Increases the number of tenants dependent on the adapter.
outcome: Adapter usage grows rather than shrinks in this period.

title: Second migration attempt stalls mid-refactor
author: eng-team
description: A second attempt to refactor tenants off the adapter was started but stalled after discovering the tenant compatibility verification step (required by ADR-014) had not been built.
decision: Pause the refactor until a compatibility verification tool exists.
constraints: No tooling existed to check tenant claim-mapping compatibility ahead of migration.
outcome: Refactor abandoned partway; adapter remains in place.

title: Tenant compatibility verification tool built
author: eng-team
description: Built a compatibility-check tool that verifies a tenant's identity provider claim mapping against the standard OAuth flow before allowing migration.
decision: All future tenant migrations off the adapter must pass this compatibility check first.
constraints: Tool must be run and pass before any tenant is migrated.
outcome: Tool adopted as a required pre-migration gate.

title: CI pipeline gains auth compatibility check step
author: platform-eng
description: CI/CD pipeline updated to run the tenant compatibility check automatically whenever changes touch auth/legacy_adapter.py, preventing accidental removal without verification.
decision: Block merges that remove adapter code paths unless compatibility check passes for all active tenants.
constraints: CI gate is required, not optional, for this file path.
outcome: No further accidental removals occurred after this gate was added.

title: Security review requires audit logging on adapter fallback
author: security-team
description: Security review required that any fallback to the legacy adapter be audit-logged, since it bypasses newer OAuth-based rate limiting.
decision: Add audit logging to all legacy adapter authentication paths.
constraints: Adapter fallback must never be silent.
outcome: Audit logging added; adapter usage now trackable per tenant.

title: Adapter identified as latency outlier under load
author: perf-team
description: Load testing identified the legacy adapter path as measurably slower than the standard OAuth flow, adding motivation to eventually retire it, but not urgency to remove it unverified.
decision: Track adapter latency as a known tradeoff; do not use performance alone as justification for removal.
constraints: Performance concerns do not override the tenant-verification requirement from ADR-014.
outcome: Logged as technical debt, not an emergency.

title: Engineering planning doc names adapter as top cognitive debt item
author: eng-team
description: Quarterly planning document lists the legacy authentication adapter as the team's top source of cognitive debt: new engineers repeatedly propose removing it without knowing the incident and ADR history behind it.
decision: Prioritize either full tenant migration or better documentation of why the adapter exists.
outcome: No action taken this quarter; adapter remains, risk of repeat mistake noted explicitly.

title: First tenant successfully migrated using compatibility tooling
author: eng-team
description: One enterprise tenant was successfully migrated off the legacy adapter after passing the compatibility check tool and a staged rollout with rollback available.
decision: Use this migration as the template process for remaining tenants.
constraints: Rollback plan must be in place before cutover for each tenant.
outcome: Migration succeeded with zero authentication incidents.

title: Migration status: majority of tenants still on legacy adapter
author: eng-team
description: Status check shows roughly 60% of enterprise SSO tenants have not yet been migrated off the legacy adapter and have not been run through the compatibility check tool.
decision: Continue tenant-by-tenant migration; do not attempt a bulk removal.
constraints: Bulk removal would violate ADR-014 for the unverified majority of tenants.
outcome: Adapter remains a required dependency for most enterprise tenants as of this check.

title: New engineer proposes removing adapter, reviewer links ADR-014
author: reviewer-5
description: A new team member opened a PR removing the legacy adapter to 'simplify the auth module.' Reviewer blocked the PR, linking ADR-014 and the 2022 incident postmortem.
decision: PR rejected pending tenant compatibility verification for all remaining tenants.
constraints: Same constraint as ADR-014: verify before removing.
outcome: PR closed; motivated later interest in tooling to prevent this recurring mistake.
